findings.description: AC-9 cannot pass against the current docs. It says 'a block is excluded only when it calls a NaruServe method absent at the wave 3 merge ... and every block not on that list compiles', and the template has only `app`, `req` and `res` in scope. Several fences in the four named files call no absent method but still cannot compile in such a template: (a) routing.md block 1 `app.route("/users/:id").get(getUser).put(updateUser).delete(deleteUser);` and the per-method priority block `app.get("/users/:id", getUser); app.get("/users/me", getMe);` use undeclared identifiers; (b) routing.md `public enum Method { GET, HEAD, ... }` and app.md `@FunctionalInterface public interface RouteHandler { ... }` are type declarations, which are illegal inside a method-body template (and would clash with the real types). None of these may go on the exclusion list, so the AC is unsatisfiable as worded. Scope also differs from I-009 ('Every JVM Java example in docs/api/'): AC-9 names only request/response/routing/app.md. Note that README.md block 2 and express-migration.md block 5 are JavaScript inside ```java fences, which would break any wider extractor.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the exclusion rule and fix the template: 'a block is excluded when it calls a NaruServe method absent at the wave 3 merge or is a type declaration that restates an API type (e.g. the Method enum, RouteHandler); the template declares any free handler identifiers (getUser, updateUser, deleteUser, getMe) as RouteHandler locals, or the docs declare them; each exclusion is listed with its reason'. Either cover every docs/api/*.md per I-009 (relabelling the JavaScript fences as ```js) or state why only the four files are in scope at wave 3.

findings.description: Still untestable in wave 3 (iter 1 F-08 was rejected, not fixed). 'The malformed-query `400` is produced after the `Request` object exists, unlike the pre-request rejections of the dispatcher' has no observable effect: wave 3 has no middleware or onError, and AC-3 already says the handler is not called. The rejection reason ('wave 4 onError/middleware makes it observable') confirms that no wave 3 test can supply evidence. An unverifiable AC blocks promotion to verified ('never promote a step requirement without verification evidence'). It is not one of the accepted limits.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove AC-4 with replace_acceptance_criteria and keep the rule as an Implementation Note via append_section_note ('the Request is built before the query is decoded; D-117/D-129 make this observable in wave 4'), or let wave 4 add the AC to its own requirement. No new seam is needed.

findings.description: No requirement says whether `res.stream(...)` blocks until the copy ends or returns while the transfer continues. FR-HTTP-016 AC-4 ('when the handler returns before the copy ends it stays STREAMING') and FR-HTTP-014 AC-5 ('including when the handler already returned') are conditional on non-blocking behaviour. A synchronous implementation, the Servlet-like default, makes those cases unreachable, so the tests either are vacuous or force an unstated design. D-103 says only that the response stays STREAMING after the handler returns.
findings.suggested_fix: State the contract in FR-HTTP-014: e.g. '`res.stream(...)` commits the response, moves it to STREAMING and returns; the dispatcher copies the stream after the handler returns, on the request thread' (or the opposite), and phrase FR-HTTP-016 AC-4 against that contract.

findings.description: AC-3 says 'A handler whose response is committed or streaming when it throws leaves the response in ABORTED'. In wave 3, `send`, `html`, `send(byte[])` and `end` take the response through COMMITTED to COMPLETED in one call (FR-HTTP-016 AC-1). So a handler that throws after `res.send("x")` meets a COMPLETED response, and abort() on a completed response 'does nothing' (FR-HTTP-015 AC-3, FR-HTTP-018 AC-3). The two ACs give different expected end states (ABORTED or COMPLETED) for this ordinary case, and the throw-after-COMPLETED outcome is not stated anywhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate AC-3 as: 'a handler that throws while the response is STREAMING leaves it ABORTED and the adapter reports an abnormal close; a handler that throws after the response is COMPLETED leaves it COMPLETED, with the sent bytes unchanged and no 500'.

findings.description: The ACs require a reflection test to find '@Nullable or @NonNull ... on every reference-type parameter and every reference-type return value'. The existing convention marks packages `@org.jspecify.annotations.NullMarked` (NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/package-info.java) and annotates only the nullable positions (e.g. Router, RouteMatch, verified CON-ROUTE-001 AC-3 'routing package is NullMarked and match carries Nullable'). Under that convention a non-null String parameter has no annotation, so the AC forces explicit @NonNull on every non-null position, which the wave 1/2 public types do not do. Two implementers could read it differently: annotate every non-null position, or rely on the package-level @NullMarked.
findings.suggested_fix: Say which form satisfies D-072: e.g. 'every reference-type parameter and return is either annotated @Nullable or lies in a @NullMarked package, so Kotlin sees no platform type (checked by AnnotatedType reflection plus the package annotation)'. Or keep the explicit-@NonNull reading and say that it deliberately departs from the @NullMarked convention.

findings.description: The over-limit failure is a plain `IOException`. Waves 5 and 6 must answer it with 413, but they cannot tell it from a transport IOException such as a connection reset. That leaves them to invent a type later, which would change this verified contract (iter 1 F-10 asked for a distinguishable type).
findings.suggested_fix: 'throws an internal IOException subclass (e.g. BodyTooLargeException) ...' so the later readers can map it to 413.

findings.description: 'a matching upgrade request gets the same `426` as a plain `GET`' is a behaviour no design item states. Router.lookup returns MATCHED with routeKind WEBSOCKET for an upgrade GET (`if (upgrade && method == Method.GET && ws != null) return matched(ws, segments, false);`), not WEBSOCKET_ONLY, so the dispatcher needs an explicit wave 3 mapping. That mapping sits only in an FR-HTTP-008 AC, not in FR-HTTP-003, which owns the result-to-status mapping.
findings.suggested_fix: Move or duplicate the rule to FR-HTTP-003 ('a MATCHED result whose routeKind is WEBSOCKET is answered 426 with the same headers until wave 7'), and add an AC that sends GET with Upgrade: websocket / Connection: Upgrade to the hook route.

findings.description: 'The checks run in this order: OPTIONS *, then the raw path not starting with / (400), then the path validator (400)'. The order of the second and third checks cannot be observed, because PathValidator.isValid itself rejects a non-'/' path (`if (!path.startsWith("/")) { return false; }`), and both checks give the same empty 400. The listed probes (`GET abc`, `GET /%2e%2e`) cannot tell the two orders apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the order in the Requirement statement and make the AC assert only observable outcomes: 'OPTIONS * gets 204 (not 400), GET abc and GET /%2e%2e get 400, and no lookup exception escapes'.

findings.description: `speckiwi validate` now reports SRS-W015 'Completed Work Log requirement is not completed: OPS-ROUTE-001' (docs/spec/91.completed-work-log.md:8), a side effect of the supersede.
findings.suggested_fix: Record in the wave 3 completed-work entry that OPS-ROUTE-001 was superseded by OPS-ROUTE-002, or accept the warning explicitly in the wave close.

summary.feasibility_check_FR-HTTP-002_AC-3: confirmed: PathValidator.isValid decodes '%252e%252e' once to '%2e%2e' (not '.'/'..', no '/', valid UTF-8) so it is accepted; Router.decodeSegments decodes once to ['%2e%2e'] and RoutePattern.match binds x='%2e%2e'. '/%2e%2e' decodes to '..' and '/a%2Fb' to 'a/b', and both are rejected.
summary.coverage: All 55 design items, the wave decisions, the carried bullets, the loop D fix (D-442) and the residual bullets are covered with the decided values. No deferred TinyHttpd half or D-392 later-wave method is required. Not re-reported: the accepted OPS-ROUTE-002 Rationale, trace rows and RoutingDocsTest re-citation.
